doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: What makes a band swing
summary: Swing is togetherness and how eighth notes are phrased, as he explains.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well along the similar lines, what makes things individually or as a rhythm section, what makes things swing?
Ooh. What makes things swing. Well it’s feeling. Hmm how could I say it. You mean technically what makes things swing?

If you were listening to a rhythm section or you were on one of those gigs just like this weekend where you get with a group and you can tell right after the first couple of times, well this band really swings, or this thing does not really swing. Is it possible to put that into words.

Yeah okay well I’ll try, now I’m understanding you better. To me, when people play together more, they’re in the same thought zone, that usually swings. And not that all swinging is the same, but it usually gets off the ground, I like to put it. You know what I mean? And it’s magic that happens. And that’s usually swinging. You know what I mean? Now the technical thing is the way they play the eighth notes. In other words,

some guys, I know I have a lot of students that come in out of high school and they think swinging is [scats]. To me you’re putting two eighth notes like more like a dotted eighth and a sixteenth. And that’s not it. It’s more of a triplet. [scats]. So that’s the technical thing. And it’s not just the drummer and the bass player, it’s also the horn players too. [scats]. That’s not it. So that adds to the not-swing. And why it’s not swing is because one guy is maybe swinging and the other guy’s going [scats] so that’s not together. So as a band that’s not happening. It’s not gelling. It’s not magic. You know what I mean? It’s not getting off the ground. It’s not leaving the earth. Okay? But when it is leaving the earth — the same with a funk band, if you’re a great funk band it’s the same thing. Boy they’re so together. You know? It lifts you right off the ground, you know what I mean? And a symphony orchestra. When it’s totally together, it’s swinging man. You know what I’m saying? It’s not swinging — that’s not what I’m talking about. I’m talking about togetherness. You know? And the world can learn a lot from that too. And politicians can learn a lot from that. The democrats and the republicans can learn a lot about that, doing it together. You know what I mean? Not I say black you say orange. I say furnace you say snowflake.
